item.title: Kotak, IndusInd, Axis Bank shares jump on strong Q2 business updates
item.description: Lenders report strong credit and deposit growth aided by FCNR(B) inflows, though analysts flag concerns over CASA momentum ...
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda
item.content:encoded: Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank, IndusInd Bank and Axis Bank rose sharply on Tuesday after the lenders reported robust growth in advances and deposits in their quarterly business updates. This growth was aided by healthy mobilisation of FCNR(B) deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank’s shares jumped 3.59 per cent to close at ₹431.25 on the BSE, while IndusInd Bank gained 2.79 per cent to end at ₹906.95. Axis Bank’s shares rose 2.01 per cent to ₹1,248.50. However, RBL Bank’s shares closed 0.72 per cent lower at ₹414 on the BSE compared with the previous day’s close. On Monday, Kotak Mahindra Bank reported robust net advances (period-end) growth of 25 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) and 13 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q). Excluding advances linked to FCNR(B) deposits, loan growth remained firm at around 21 per cent Y-o-Y and 10 per cent Q-o-Q. Deposits grew 23 per cent Y-o-Y and 14 per cent Q-o-Q, aided by FCNR(B) inflows. Excluding these, deposit growth was more measured at 13 per cent Y-o-Y and 4 per cent Q-o-Q. Current account savings account (CASA) balances grew 11 per cent Y-o-Y and 8 per cent Q-o-Q. The bank mobilised $5.78 billion through FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter. Axis Bank, India’s third-largest private sector lender, said its deposits grew 5.8 per cent sequentially and 20.7 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹14.52 trillion as of September 30, while gross advances rose 8.8 per cent Q-o-Q and 22.7 per cent YoY to ₹13.85 trillion. The lender mobilised $10.62 billion (₹1.02 trillion) in FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India’s swap facility introduced earlier this year.   “While the outcome is good on the loan growth front, the question is sustainability plus core deposit growth around 12-13 per cent for Kotak (Mahindra Bank) and Axis (Bank) isn’t that great. That goes to show that eventually loan growth will have to come down from current levels. CASA growth is also 10 to 11 per cent similar to HDFC Bank showing the pressure that exists in CASA across the system. CASA ratios continue to decline even on core deposit growth basis”, said Suresh Ganapathy, MD&Head - Financial Services Research, Macquarie Capital.  Meanwhile, IndusInd Bank’s net advances grew 11.2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3.62 trillion as of September 30, 2026, outpacing the 10.1 per cent growth in deposits to ₹4.29 trillion. IndusInd Bank’s CASA ratio declined to 28 per cent from 30.7 per cent a year earlier and 29.4 per cent in June. The lender mobilised $3.51 billion in FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI’s deposit swap facility, with outstanding loans of about ₹16,564 crore extended from its GIFT City branch against these deposits as of September-end. And, RBL Bank’s total deposits rose 34 per cent Y-o-Y to around ₹1.56 trillion in the quarter ended September 30 (Q2FY27), while gross advances grew 40 per cent to around ₹1.43 trillion. (Disclosure: Entities controlled by the Kotak family have a significant holding in Business Standard Pvt Ltd)

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Paramount completes Warner Bros merger to form Hollywood giant Skydance

Paramount completes Warner Bros merger to form Hollywood giant Skydance The combined company will carry about $80 billion in debt, while co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz face a target of delivering $6 billion in planned cost savings

In just 16 years, Skydance has gone from an independent studio to the centre of one of Hollywood's biggest power plays | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 06 2026 | 6:33 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Paramount Skydance on Tuesday completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, creating a Hollywood heavyweight called Skydance and handing CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's largest entertainment companies.   The deal brings together the studios behind "Mission: Impossible," "Harry Potter" and DC Studios alongside major television and streaming networks such as CBS, CNN, Paramount+ and HBO Max — forming an expansive entertainment company spanning film, TV and news.   Shares of the combined company moved to the New York Stock Exchange from Nasdaq on Tuesday to trade under the ticker "SKYD."   Settlements with a coalition of US states and a Hollywood writers union removed the main legal barriers to the merger, one of the largest in media history. It comes as Hollywood faces declining cable-TV subscriptions, the high cost of competing for streaming audiences and persistent pressure from unions over jobs and creative workers' rights.

Ellison said last week the Skydance name was chosen to retain the individual identities of Paramount and Warner Bros studios, rather than combining them under a new brand. Also Read

US judge approves settlement, clearing $81 bn Paramount-Warner Bros. merger

Paramount-Warner $81 bn merger clears key hurdle as states settle lawsuits

Paramount settles US states' lawsuit over $110 bn Warner Bros merger

Paramount settlement talks include penalty for missing 30-film pledge

Paramount settlement talks include plan to keep company in California

Analysts, however, said the name reinforces the extent of Ellison's control, highlighting how some of Hollywood's most iconic brands now answer to him and how he has a platform to impose his strategy and culture.   In just 16 years, Skydance has gone from an independent studio to the centre of one of Hollywood's biggest power plays.   Founded in 2010 by the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, it built its reputation as a financial backer and producer of Paramount's blockbuster "Top Gun: Maverick." After merging with Paramount last year, Skydance set its sights on Warner Bros, entering a heated bidding contest with Netflix while drawing interest from other potential suitors, including Comcast.

Broader hollywood bet   Ellison named Mattel's former CEO Ynon Kreiz as Skydance co-CEO to run day-to-day operations and lead the integration, while Ellison oversees creative direction and overall strategy.   The duo faces the task of combining two large companies while delivering $6 billion in planned cost savings, a big part of which Paramount said would come from "non-labour sources" — by combining streaming technologies and cloud providers of the two companies. However, the scale of the cuts is expected to affect jobs across Hollywood.   The combined company is also expected to carry about $80 billion in debt, putting pressure on Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cash flow from cable networks and improve theatrical film performance.

CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss would continue in their respective leadership roles at Skydance.

item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Trent emerges Nifty superstar with 12% gain after strong Q2 update

Trent emerges Nifty superstar with 12% gain after strong Q2 update Trent shares jumped 12.4 per cent after Q2FY27 standalone revenue rose 22.5 per cent, beating estimates, while analysts remained largely bullish on the Tata group retailer

Analysts and brokers have mixed views on whether growth will be back for the company

Shilpa Rangarajan Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 06 2026 | 9:32 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Shares of Tata group retailer Trent surged 12.4 per cent on Tuesday, taking centre stage as the benchmark indices extended their rebound to a second straight session after eight consecutive weeks of heavy selling.   The stock closed at ₹2,900 after the company's business update for the second quarter (July-September) of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27) showed standalone revenue rising 22.5 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to ₹5,788 crore. According to Bernstein, that was its fastest growth in six quarters, ahead of the 18.5 per cent consensus estimate. Bernstein said that Trent added 30 net stores in the quarter — including 17 Zudio and 10 Westside outlets — taking its fashion store count to 1,342.

In a world of online buyers, retail is one segment still valued by the number of physical stores a company adds every year. Trent has always been ahead at this game. Until December 2024, each new store added about ₹630 crore to the company’s market cap. Investors were paying for future growth, not just the stores already open. Since December 2024, the relationship has flipped. Every additional store has come with about ₹240 crore less market cap. Store openings didn't destroy value but the market has cut the price it pays for each store as sales per store weakened.   Trent's market value per Zudio and Westside store fell from a peak of ₹290 crore in December 2024 to ₹104.2 crore by September 2026, even as their combined count rose to 1,342 from 873, showed Bloomberg data, the company’s reports, and exchange filings.

Motilal Oswal, which gives the stock a "Buy" rating, said that Q1FY27 revenue per store fell just 1 per cent Y-o-Y compared to a 5 per cent decline previously, indicating that the impact of cannibalisation is easing. Also Read

Strong revenue growth powers GCPL's Q2 show, margins remain in focus premium

Newly-listed Steamhouse India hits 10% upper circuit after Q1 results

Airfare strength to offset fuel cost in Q2; IndiGo PAT may rise 176%: Elara

Reliance Industries gains 3% as Jio IPO plan fuels hopes of value unlocking

“I think if the stock manages to sustain above 2,900-2,925 levels on closing basis, then there are brighter chances that it may further scale up to 3,100-3,300 levels,” said Gaurav Sharma, head of research, Globe Capital.   Trent, however, still trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 76, up from 68 a year ago. Over the past five years, the stock has given a 31 per cent annualised return, vastly outperforming the Nifty 50's 5 per cent.

Analysts and brokers have mixed views on whether growth will be back for the company.   Vincent K Andrews, senior research analyst at Geojit Investments, said: "The improvement in the revenue growth supported the current premium valuation, but still it is at premium.” He expects growth to improve further if store additions stay strong.   Brokerages remain largely bullish. Of the 29 analysts tracking the stock on Bloomberg, 22 rate it “Buy”, five “Hold”, and two “Sell”. Their average target price of ₹3,417.57 implies an upside of about 18 per cent.   Citi is the only brokerage with an outright “Sell” rating and a target below ₹3,000, at ₹2,950. "We remain cautious on Trent given a still-weak revenue per square foot (sq ft) trend, increasing competition, impact of cannibalisation, and risk to margins from input cost inflation," it said. Kotak Institutional Equities, the other bear, rates the stock “Reduce”, with a target of ₹3,150.

Morgan Stanley, which has an “Overweight” rating and a target of ₹3,406, said: "Better-than-expected revenue growth, especially in the context of the shift in the festive calendar, should be viewed positively."   Bernstein retained its “Outperform” rating and ₹3,500 target. It noted that the growth surprise came in a quarter when other value-apparel retailers struggled because the festive season shifted from the second to the third quarter.   More From This Section
